questions.statement: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
questions.context: Pasiva, San Juan, grado 11.

options.feedback: Without 'be' this is not a passive form; the verb reads as intransitive.
'Is building' is an active progressive, not a passive.
The reflexive adds no passive auxiliary here.
'Was built' is 'be' plus participle, the passive pattern.

questions.explanation:
La voz pasiva se construye con 'be' seguido del participio, y el agente suele aparecer con 'by'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Change to the passive: 'Someone stole my bicycle.'
questions.context: Transformacion a la pasiva, Ponce, grado 11.

options.feedback: 'Was stolen' places the object in the subject position.
The simple past cannot follow 'is' in a passive form.
This reads as an active verb with the bicycle as agent.
'Stealing' is a gerund, not the required past participle.

questions.explanation:
El objeto 'my bicycle' pasa a sujeto y el verbo 'stole' se convierte en participio con 'was'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'The report ____ by the committee next week.'
questions.context: Pasiva con tiempo futuro, Mayaguez, grado 11.

options.feedback: That is the active form with the subject doing the submitting.
'Will be' plus participle is the future passive structure.
The present continuous is not a future passive.
The simple past passive refers to a past event.

questions.explanation:
Una pasiva futura se forma con 'will be' mas el participio del verbo principal. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the passive equivalent of 'They must finish the project today'?
questions.context: Pasiva con modales, Humacao, grado 11.

options.feedback: A participle cannot follow the modal directly; 'be' is needed.

options.text: The project must being finished today.
options.feedback: 'Must being' is not grammatical.

options.text: The project must have finish today.
options.feedback: A bare base form cannot follow 'have' in a passive.

options.text: The project must be finished today.
options.feedback: 'Must be' plus participle is the modal passive pattern.

questions.explanation:
En pasiva el modal se mantiene y el verbo principal pasa a participio preceded by 'be'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: 'The window was broken during the storm.' What can you infer?
questions.context: Inferencia sobre la pasiva, Caguas, grado 11.

options.feedback: Naming the agent would require a 'by' phrase.
The passive does not imply absence of an agent.
That reading has no basis in the sentence.
The passive omits the doer when no 'by' phrase appears.

questions.explanation:
La pasiva oculta al agente, por lo que solo sabemos que alguien rompio la ventana durante la tormenta.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'The cake was ate by the children.' What is the error?
questions.context: Deteccion de errores, Arecibo, grado 11.

options.feedback: The passive requires the past participle.

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: Using the simple past after 'was' is a standard passive error.
The subject 'cake' is singular, so 'was' is correct.
'By' is optional in the passive but not incorrect here.

questions.explanation:
Tras 'was' en pasiva debe aparecer el participio pasado 'eaten', no el pasado simple 'ate'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is in the passive voice with a modal perfective?
questions.context: Pasiva con 'should have', Guaynabo, grado 11.

options.text: The letter should have signed earlier.
options.feedback: That form is active and assigns the signing to the letter.

options.text: The letter should been signed earlier.
options.feedback: 'Should been' lacks the required infinitive marker.

options.text: The letter should have been signed earlier.
options.feedback: 'Should have been' plus participle is the modal perfective passive.

options.text: The letter should being signed earlier.
options.feedback: 'Should being' is not a valid sequence.

questions.explanation:
'Should have been' mas participio forma una pasiva con modal y aspecto perfecto. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.context: Pasiva con 'has been', Vega Baja, grado 11.

options.feedback: 'Has been' plus participle gives the present perfect passive.
That is the active form with the environment as agent.
'Has being' is not grammatical in this structure.
The simple past passive refers to a completed past situation.

questions.explanation:
'Has been' mas participio forma la pasiva del presente perfecto. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.statement: What is the passive form of 'They are painting the school'?
questions.context: Pasiva en presente continuo, Jayuya, grado 11.

options.feedback: That is the simple present passive, not the continuous.
That reads as an active verb with the school as agent.
'Is being' plus participle is the present continuous passive.
A base form cannot follow 'being' in this structure.

questions.explanation:
La pasiva del presente continuo se forma con 'is being' mas participio. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which statement about the passive voice is correct?
questions.context: Marco conceptual, Yauco, grado 11.

options.text: It emphasises the object or patient rather than the doer
options.feedback: That is the pragmatic function of the passive.

options.text: It is used only when the agent is unknown
options.feedback: It also emphasises an unknown or irrelevant agent, but that is not its only use.

options.text: It changes the tense of the verb
options.feedback: The tense is marked by 'be', which does not itself change it.
The 'by' phrase is optional and often omitted.

questions.explanation:
La pasiva devuelve el enfasis al objeto o al paciente de la accion en lugar del agente.

questions.statement: Complete: 'These books ____ in the library; you cannot take them out.'
questions.context: Pasiva con modal de prohibicion, Barceloneta, grado 11.

options.feedback: That is the active form and assigns the taking to the books.
A base form cannot follow 'be' in a passive.
'Must not be' plus participle expresses the prohibition in the passive.
The participle form requires 'be' after the modal.

questions.explanation:
Una prohibicion en pasiva se forma con 'must not be' mas participio. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: 'The results will be announced on Friday.' What is the passive form used for here?
questions.context: Analisis del uso, Maunabo, grado 11.

options.text: The speaker does not know the agent
options.feedback: That is only one of several reasons to use the passive.

options.text: The action has not happened yet
options.feedback: That is expressed by 'will', not by the passive voice.

options.text: The results were announced in the past
options.feedback: The sentence is in the future passive.

options.text: The agent is unimportant; the timing is the focus
options.feedback: The passive foreground the event rather than the person behind it.

questions.explanation:
Se usa la pasiva porque no importa quien anuncia los resultados, sino cuando se Bride.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correctly formed in the passive voice?
questions.context: Interrogacion pasiva, Naguabo, grado 11.

options.text: Did the letter was delivered yesterday?
options.feedback: Auxiliary 'did' cannot be combined with the passive 'was'.
The present perfect cannot refer to a finished past moment such as 'yesterday'.
'Was' leads the question and 'delivered' is the participle.
Without an auxiliary at the front it is not a question.

questions.explanation:
En pasiva la pregunta conserva el auxiliar 'be' al inicio seguido del participio. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.statement: Complete: 'The decision ____ by the board before the announcement.'
questions.context: Pasiva con 'before', Ciales, grado 11.

options.feedback: The simple past alone does not mark the passive voice.
'Was taken' places the decision as completed before the announcement.
'Has' requires a participle, not a base form.
A base form cannot follow 'was' in a passive.

questions.explanation:
Una accion terminada antes de otra se expresa en pasiva con 'was' mas participio. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'These houses are build in 1920.' What is the error?
questions.context: Deteccion de errores, Juana Diaz, grado 11.

options.feedback: The passive requires the past participle 'built'.

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: The base form after 'are' is a standard error.
'Houses' is plural, so 'are' is the correct auxiliary.
The year is arbitrary and is not the error.

questions.explanation:
El participio pasado de 'build' es 'built'; despues de 'are' no se usa la forma base.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the passive with a 'by' phrase correctly?
questions.context: Agente en la pasiva, Luquillo, grado 11.

options.text: The bridge was designed of a famous architect.
options.feedback: 'Of' cannot introduce the agent of a passive verb.

options.text: The bridge was designed with a famous architect.
options.feedback: 'With' names an instrument or tool, not the agent.

options.text: The bridge was designed by a famous architect.
options.feedback: 'By' introduces the agent, the architect.

options.text: The bridge was designed for a famous architect.
options.feedback: 'For' marks a purpose or a recipient, not the agent.

questions.explanation:
La preposicion 'by' introduce al agente responsable de la accion en la pasiva. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.context: Pasiva con futuro perfecto, Cayey, grado 11.

options.feedback: That is the active form and makes the work the agent.

options.text: The work will been completed by then.

options.text: A passive sentence with an unidentified agent
options.feedback: 'Were made' is the passive pair and no 'by' phrase appears.

options.text: A sentence with a modal verb
options.feedback: No modal is used here.

options.text: The active always sounds more formal
